source.title: A Reparameterization-Invariant Flatness Measure for Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Henning Petzka; Linara Adilova; Michael Kamp; C. Sminchisescu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is the full paper. The appendix contains a few apparent equation-reference placeholders, but they do not affect the reported experiments.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether flatness measures track the training–generalization error gap using a newly proposed reparameterization-invariant measure and empirical correlations.
record.gate_note: Reports correlations between flatness measures and generalization error for trained networks; these are measurements of a property named in V7. The paper does not test random-label memorization, width beyond interpolation, architecture comparisons, optimizer generalization, batch-size effects on test performance, dropout, or example removal. Cited results are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study correlates norm-scaled Hessian measures with a training–test loss gap. It does not measure V7's magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance before training error rises. These related sharpness measures do not establish whether the specified measure tracks generalization. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate: the authors report strong correlations between their proposed flatness measures and generalization loss gaps, and prove invariance to function-preserving layer rescaling. They acknowledge that the layer-wise measures are not generally invariant to neuron-wise rescaling and introduce additional measures addressing that limitation.
record.recipe_differences: Measures Hessian-based flatness and its correlation with generalization error across training configurations; it does not perform the magnitude-scaled weight perturbation tolerance comparison described in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured correlation varies slightly by hidden layer for the MNIST layer-wise measures and may differ considerably by layer for the neuron-wise measures. Layer-wise reparameterization leaves the proposed CIFAR10 measures correlated while Hessian-only measures have very weak correlation.

fits_no_version.finding: For LeNet5 on CIFAR-10, both layer-norm-scaled Hessian measures correlate with the loss gap; the trace-based measure has correlation 0.91. Layer rescaling preserves these measures while weakening Hessian-only correlations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Layer-norm-scaled Hessian sharpness can correlate with generalization loss gaps while remaining invariant to function-preserving layer rescaling.

fits_no_version.finding: For the fully connected MNIST network, layer-wise trace measures have correlations of at least 0.7; neuron-based correlations vary by layer, and network aggregates reportedly correlate more strongly.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The association between Hessian-based sharpness and generalization loss gaps depends on the measure and its aggregation across layers.

record.peer_reviewed: Workshop Science meets Engineering of Deep Learning, 33rd Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2019)
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported. Correlations are described as significant or strong but generally lack exact coefficients; several findings are presented through figures without numerical values in the text. The experiments use one CIFAR10 architecture and one MNIST fully connected architecture, and the reported association is correlational.
record.rows_left_out: No additional distinct results on the tested version were omitted.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting alongside natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label test accuracy.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer performance under specified tuning regimes.
Large-batch held-out performance under matched epoch budgets and adapted training recipes; varying batches to obtain different minima does not supply this comparison.
Effects of dropout and its removal on held-out error.

Magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance before training error rises, its association with error gaps among similarly fitted convolutional networks, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The reported correlations remain valid findings, but they concern related measures outside the supplied versions. Numerical coefficients embedded in figures cannot be independently recovered from the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Widening beyond the interpolation threshold and resulting test error.
Large-batch generalization under epoch budgets and adapted recipes.

The tested measures are Hessian-based flatness measures, including the proposed layer-wise norm-scaled measures; the study does not test magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance as phrased in the version, compare against the version's stated norm- and margin-based measures, or establish causality.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation between last-hidden-layer flatness κ5 and generalization error across trained configurations.

conditions.value: Xavier normal, Kaiming uniform, uniform in (−0.1, 0.1), normal with µ = 0 and σ² = 0.1

rows.measure: Correlation between κ5 and approximated generalization error (test error minus training error).
rows.note: The text describes the correlation as significant; it gives the exact coefficient only for κ5τ, in R2.
rows.check: Measures layer-norm-scaled maximum Hessian eigenvalue, not V7's perturbation tolerance. The gap uses loss values, specifically five times summed test loss minus summed training loss.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation between last-hidden-layer trace-based flatness κ5τ and generalization error across trained configurations.

conditions.value: Xavier normal, Kaiming uniform, uniform in (−0.1, 0.1), normal with µ = 0 and σ² = 0.1

rows.measure: Correlation between κ5τ and approximated generalization error (test error minus training error).
rows.note: The authors state this correlation is stronger than for κ5.
rows.check: The reported correlation of 0.91 concerns layer-norm-scaled Hessian trace and a loss gap, not V7's specified measure.

rows.subject: LeNet5
rows.stage_stated: trained till convergence; randomly reparameterized after training
rows.operation_detail: Compared the proposed flatness measures with Hessian-only measures after layer-wise reparameterization.
rows.measure: Correlation with generalization error after reparameterization.
rows.baseline: Correlation before reparameterization; exact value not stated
rows.value: Proposed measures are not affected; traditional Hessian-only measures have very weak correlation after modifications.
rows.note: The proposed measure's correlation persists under this tested reparameterization; Hessian-only measures lose correlation. The text does not provide exact values.
rows.check: Combines preserved correlations for proposed measures with weakened correlations for Hessian-only measures. Neither measures V7's perturbation tolerance; failure of unscaled Hessian measures does not challenge magnitude-aware sharpness.

rows.subject: Custom fully connected network with ReLU activations
rows.size_stated: 4 hidden layers with 50, 50, 50, and 30 neurons; output layer has 10 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Measured layer-wise trace-based flatness and its correlation with generalization error for each hidden layer.

conditions.value: Xavier normal scheme with random seed
0.02 to 1.6 correspondingly to keep the ratio constant
configurations with larger than 0.07 training error were filtered out

rows.measure: Correlation between each hidden layer's trace-based flatness and generalization error.
rows.note: Correlation is reported as strong for all four hidden layers; the authors say it varies slightly by layer.
rows.check: Measures Hessian-trace correlations in a fully connected MNIST network, not V7's specified perturbation measure. The text's claim of constant learning-rate/batch-size ratio is inconsistent with its listed endpoints; preserve that ambiguity.

rows.subject: Custom fully connected network with ReLU activations
rows.size_stated: 4 hidden layers with 50, 50, 50, and 30 neurons; output layer has 10 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation between neuron-wise flatness measure ρlσ and generalization error for each hidden layer.
rows.measure: Correlation between ρlσ and generalization error.
rows.note: The text calls the correlation significant but notes that it might differ considerably depending on the layer.
rows.check: Measures a sum of neuron-level Hessian quadratic forms, not V7's perturbation tolerance. Layer dependence alone does not establish a partial effect for V7.

rows.subject: Custom fully connected network with ReLU activations
rows.size_stated: 4 hidden layers with 50, 50, 50, and 30 neurons; output layer has 10 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Measured correlation between neuron-wise flatness measure ρl and generalization error for each hidden layer.
rows.measure: Correlation between ρl and generalization error.
rows.note: The text calls the correlation significant but notes that it might differ considerably depending on the layer.
rows.check: Measures a maximum of neuron-level Hessian quadratic forms, not V7's perturbation tolerance. Layer dependence alone does not establish a partial effect for V7.

rows.subject: Custom fully connected network with ReLU activations
rows.size_stated: 4 hidden layers with 50, 50, 50, and 30 neurons; output layer has 10 neurons
rows.operation_detail: Measured network-wise correlations for combined flatness measures κmaxτ, κΣτ, ρmax, and ρΣ.
rows.measure: Correlation of each network-wise measure with generalization error.
rows.baseline: Original neuron-wise and layer-wise measures; exact values not stated
rows.value: Each network-wise measure has a larger correlation with generalization loss than the original neuron-wise and layer-wise measures; exact values not stated.
rows.note: The text states the comparison but does not give coefficients.
rows.check: Compares correlations among the authors' aggregated Hessian measures. It does not compare V7's specified sharpness measure with norm- and margin-based measures.
